# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the AMG benchmark on a single AWS ARM-based Kubernetes node.
# It is configured for a test run with a small problem size.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Using an incrementing name to avoid collisions on subsequent runs.
  name: amg-aws-cpu-test-1
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster. For this test, we start with 1.
  size: 1

  # Define the main application container. There should only be one.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to execute. The Flux operator will wrap this with flux run/submit.
      # Runs AMG problem 2 with a small 4x4x4 problem size for testing.
      command: amg -problem 2 -P 4 4 4
      # The launcher pod is the broker, not an application pod. This MUST be false.
      launcher: false
      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

  # Flux-specific configuration section.
  flux:
    # Set the architecture to ARM as required for the AWS instance type.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Use the ARM-compatible flux-view image, as instructed.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # strict mode ensures all output is captured.
    strict: true

  # Set cleanup to false to allow for inspection of logs and resources after the job completes.
  cleanup: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest addresses the task count mismatch from the previous attempt.
# It is configured to run the AMG benchmark on a single AWS ARM-based Kubernetes node.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Incrementing the name to avoid collisions with the previous attempt.
  name: amg-aws-cpu-test-2
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster remains 1, as we are testing on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Explicitly set the number of tasks required by the application (4*4*4=64).
  # This corrects the error where only 1 task was being launched by default.
  tasks: 64

  # Define the main application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command remains the same, requesting a 4x4x4 processor topology.
      command: amg -problem 2 -P 4 4 4
      # The launcher pod is the broker, not an application pod. This MUST be false.
      launcher: false
      # Environment variables to configure single-threading and enable EFA for MPI communication.
      environment:
        OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: "cma"
        FI_PROVIDER: "efa"
        FI_EFA_USE_DEVICE_RDMA: "1"
      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

  # Flux-specific configuration section.
  flux:
    # Set the architecture to ARM as required for the AWS instance type.
    arch: "arm"
    # Additional flags passed to flux start, enabling CPU affinity per task for performance.
    optionFlags: "-o cpu-affinity=per-task"
    container:
      # Use the ARM-compatible flux-view image, as instructed.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # strict mode ensures all output is captured.
    strict: true

  # Set cleanup to false to allow for inspection of logs and resources after the job completes.
  cleanup: false
